The 2019 Arctic Council Ministerial Meeting salvaged one potentially useful initiative concerning Arctic Ocean governance. The Council decided to create an “SAO-based mechanism” — SAO referring to diplomats who serve as Senior Arctic Officials and represent each state within the council — intended to co-ordinate the council’s efforts on marine issues. Unfortunately, the pandemic delayed the first meeting of this body, originally scheduled for early 2020. The meeting instead took place virtually in September and October, with limited results. It is difficult to say what will come of the SAO-based mechanism (now referred to as the SMM).22
